meaningChecks: Day1 professional roles remain distinct: care worker cannot diagnose or treat; suspected swallowing difficulty is referred to nurse/ST, not independently trained. Explicit medical-professional reporting recipient is retained in infection observation.
Day2 cleaning consent is separate from consent to move belongings; chair location, prohibition on shelf placement and return of both newspaper and glasses remain explicit.
Day3 physical assistance does not remove self-determination. Writing, reading an address slowly in chunks, and checking after writing remain assigned to the correct person.

Day4 private setting does not authorize broader information sharing. Daughter-specific contact and responsible-worker sharing remain separately scoped, with prior agreement about content. Abuse categories and team reporting preserve observed/inferred distinction.

Day5 participation wish and photography refusal remain separate. Unknown seat/method is not promised; participant makes the final choice after conditions are confirmed. Care process includes assessment, plan, implementation and evaluation rather than only a completion mark.

Day6 room-use time and return deadline remain separate, with unknown deadline assigned to Kishimoto for checking. Infection precautions retain all-user scope, task-dependent PPE, hand hygiene after glove removal, facility/product instructions and uncertainty about pathogens.

Day7 own reading remains the person’s activity; requested page-finding and absence notification stay with the worker. Body mechanics does not authorize solo lifting; individual plan, pain, equipment instructions, training, staffing and lift preference remain explicit.
All 59 questions have four individually translated, specific option rationales. Correct answer positions, negation, sequence, uncertainty and clinical limits are unchanged.

Preserved Japanese headwords/kana in educational vocabulary entries and the named normalization concept; all prose meaning is in Khmer. No pivot-language teaching prose or placeholders.
